title: Understanding Pipe Slope in Drainage Systems
description: Gravity is the primary driving force in non-pressure drainage systems, making proper pipe slope essential for effective waste transport. Horizontal drainage piping must be installed with a consistent downward grade toward the main sewer. If the slope is too flat, liquid wastes move too slowly, allowing solid particulate to settle and form blockages over time. Conversely, if the slope is excessively steep, water runs away too quickly from heavier solids, leaving waste behind in the pipe. Maintaining the correct grade ensures a self-cleansing velocity where both liquids and solids travel smoothly through the system.
